questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence In passive voice.

He has not committed the crime.

options.text: The crime was not committed by him.
The crime have not being committed by him.
The crime have not been committed by him.
The crime has not been committed by him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**The crime has not been committed by him.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In passive voice, **the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence**.

 
 
• Example: I am loved by him.
 
 
 
• Now, in the given sentence, 
 
 
• The auxiliary verb "has" changes to "has been" in the passive voice.
 
• The past participle form of the main verb "commit" is "committed."
 
• The preposition "by" is used to indicate the doer of the action in the passive voice.
 
 
 
• Thus, the sentence in passive voice will be: The crime has not been committed by him.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Binay said that / he is coming / from / his village, Jaygarh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**he is coming**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is a reported speech, which indicates that the action was stated in the past.
 
• Therefore, the verb tenses should align with the context of reported past action.
 
• The phrase "**Binay said that**" triggers the need for backshifting the tense in the reported clause, meaning that present tenses in direct speech are generally changed to their past tense forms in reported speech.
 
• The correct tense to use in this context would be "**was coming**" instead of "**is coming**" to match the past tense narrative set by "**said that**."
 
• Consistency in tense usage is crucial for maintaining grammatical correctness and ensuring clarity in communication.
 
• Using "**is coming**" in this context disrupts the temporal coherence of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1) "**from**" has no error in itself. This preposition is correctly used to indicate the origin of someone's journey.
 
• Option 3) "**his village, Jaygarh**" is a phrase providing additional information about the origin and is correctly structured with the use of a comma for apposition. There's no grammatical error in this segment.
 
• Option 4) "**Binay said that**" correctly introduces reported speech. The use of "said that" is appropriate for indicating that the narrative is recounting something Binay communicated in the past.

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. In 1944, he was honoured by King George VI with a Knighthood and became Sir Alexander Fleming.

B. On receiving this great honour, Fleming said in his usual modest way, “Wherever I go, people thank me for saving their lives. I didn’t do anything; I Just found a remedy that was there.”

C. Fleming became famous overnight and was regarded as one of the most distinguished scientists of his time.

D. The next year, he and his fellow bacteriologists, whose combined efforts had led to the great discovery, were honoured with a joint Nobel Prize.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**CADB.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To connect the given sentence in a chronological order. We must find out the central theme of the passage.
 
• The central theme or the subject of the passage is " the scientist named Fleming."
 
 
• Sentence C talks about Fleming becoming famous overnight and being regarded as one of the most distinguished scientists of his time.
 
• Later on, the sentence A mentions Fleming being honoured with a Knighthood by King George VI in 1944.
 
• Further, sentence D talks about Fleming and his fellow bacteriologists being honoured with a joint Nobel Prize the next year.
 
• Sentence B contains a quote from Fleming where he expresses his modesty despite all the recognition he received.
 
• Sentence, B has a closing tone to it. Thus, it will be placed at the end.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct order is "CADB."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

She was waiting for a opportunity to start her own business.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**for a opportunity**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the part "for a opportunity."
 
• **The correct phrase is "for an opportunity" because "opportunity" starts with a vowel sound.**
 
• Using "a" before a word starting with a vowel sound is a common mistake in English.
 
• **We use "an" before a word starting with a vowel sound.**
 
• Thus, the correct article to use is "an" and the correct phrase is "for an opportunity."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

**Corrected sentence**: "She was waiting for **an **opportunity to start her own business."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The players distributed the reward __between themselves __
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**among themselves**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the word "between" is used incorrectly.
 
• **"Between" is used when there are only two people or things involved.**
 
 
• Example: The metro remains closed between 1 AM and 4 AM.
 
 
 
• **"Among" is used when there are three or more**.
 
 
• Example: She is among those who survived.
 
 
 
• ** "Themselves" is the correct reflexive pronoun to use in this sentence. It is used to emphasize "they."**
 
• Thus, the correct word to use with "themselves" will be "among."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1, "between them", is grammatically incorrect because it suggests there are only two players involved.
 
• Option 3, "between their selves", is incorrect because the reflexive pronoun should be "themselves".
 
• Option 4, "amongst their self", is incorrect because it uses the singular form "self" instead of the plural "selves".
